newsitem.title: UK: BOE'S KING SAYS RATE PAUSE NEED NOT END WITH RISE.
newsitem.headline: BOE'S KING SAYS RATE PAUSE NEED NOT END WITH RISE.

text.p: Bank of England deputy governor Mervyn King said on Wednesday it was not certain that a pause in UK interest rate moves would end with a rate rise.

Asked at a news conference whether the central issue was the timing and extent of another rise in interest rates, King said: "No I don't think you can come to that conclusion because the committee always takes it one month at a time."
King added, "And we have not decided that the next move in interest rates would be upward and that the only uncertain factor is how long we wait."
British official interest rates, which last week were increased to seven percent, have risen four times in as many months.
King was speaking following release of a Bank of England inflation report
